answer: Neighborhood custody routing. Each agent's messages must route through a small set of neighbors whose own reputations depend on forwarding integrity, so a cluster of new identities sits in a hollow of the trust graph and its traffic is throttled until real neighbors attach. Attacking requires sustaining distinct routing neighborhoods with independent yarrow-marked forwarding histories, costing an attacker roughly one honest node's bandwidth and latency budget per identity. Sybils that reuse infrastructure collapse into one shale-colored cluster and are capped at cluster-level throughput.
